open_points.subject: store.record_change and mutable Run state
open_points.text: “a lifecycle change of another entity (a status, who decided or resolved or released and when, `concluded_at`) updates those fields of the entity's one record in place ... every other field is never changed” conflicts with `record_run_progress`, which writes “the run's status, outputs, WaitingPoints M20, `ended_at`, `cancelled_by`”, and `record_resumption`, which adds a resumption.
open_points.question: Which Run fields may be updated after `start_run`, and are outputs, waiting points and resumptions fields of the Run record or separate records?
options: Permit every mutation explicitly named by `record_run_progress`, `record_resumption` and `release_run`
Keep the Run record immutable except for the listed lifecycle fields and store outputs, waiting points and resumptions as separate records
open_points.default_guess: Permit the mutations named by the store changes, while keeping the run's identity, pins, inputs, starter and start time immutable.

open_points.subject: owner access to trial file fixtures
open_points.text: A07 says “The owner receives every value” and distinguishes personal-data files, but State 5 says “a file — StoredValue fixture or SpooledFile — as digest, size and media type, its bytes only through `read_spooled_file`”, while `read_spooled_file` “takes only a SpooledFile — never a StoredValue”.
open_points.question: Can the owner read the bytes of a trial-case file fixture, and if so through which operation?
options: Allow an owner-only operation to read file-carriage StoredValues
Extend `read_spooled_file` to accept file-carriage StoredValues
Intentionally expose fixture metadata only and narrow the earlier owner-disclosure promise
open_points.default_guess: Allow the owner to read file-carriage StoredValues through a dedicated or generalized byte-read surface operation.

open_points.subject: functions.add_trial_case file inputs
open_points.text: Its inputs are only “input values by port, optional expected outputs”, although trial cases may contain file fixtures and the flow says “Value bytes and file fixtures go to the content-addressed area”.
open_points.question: How are authored input and expected-output file fixtures supplied to `functions.add_trial_case`: raw bytes, a byte stream, or digest/size/media-type facts referencing bytes already stored somewhere?
options: Supply raw bytes with media type
Supply a bounded byte stream with media type
Supply an existing StoredValue identity
open_points.default_guess: Supply raw bytes with the port supplying the media type; the function computes the digest and stores the fixture.

open_points.subject: TrialCase expected_outputs
open_points.text: M06 says “`expected_outputs`: StoredValues by output port ... absent when only the absence of failure is required”, while `functions.add_trial_case` takes “optional expected outputs” without saying whether a present set must contain every output port.
open_points.question: When `expected_outputs` is present, must it contain exactly every contract output, or may it assert only a subset?
options: Exactly every output port
Any non-empty subset of output ports
Each output is independently optional
open_points.default_guess: Require exactly every output port when `expected_outputs` is present.

open_points.subject: FlowConstant schema
open_points.text: `flows.compose_flow_version` takes “constants with declared classes”, but its enforcement says “A constant's StoredValue takes the `value_schema` and class the composing agent declared with it”, even though no constant schema is named among the inputs and the target port may be missing.
open_points.question: Where does a constant's `value_schema` come from?
options: The composition request explicitly declares it on each constant
It is copied from the target port
It is inferred from the literal value
open_points.default_guess: Require each constant to declare its own `value_schema`, because proof must remain possible when its target is missing.

open_points.subject: installation.load_installation validation
open_points.text: The operation says it enforces only “A regular private file of the kernel's user, not a link; tokens of at least 43 characters, pairwise distinct”, while M27 says repeated agent names are refused at start and A17 says a credential header that is not an HTTP field-name token also refuses startup.
open_points.question: Which start-time configuration checks belong to `load_installation`, including unique agent names and credential-header syntax?
options: `load_installation` performs all configuration-only checks from M27 and A17
Another named start operation performs the omitted checks
The omitted checks are intentionally no longer required
open_points.default_guess: Have `load_installation` enforce unique agent names and credential-header syntax in addition to the checks already listed.

open_points.subject: store.open_store initialization
open_points.text: It says “Take the exclusive lock, check the data directory and remove temporary files” and returns “An open store”, but does not say what happens when the configured directory, database, or storage subdirectories do not yet exist.
open_points.question: Does `open_store` initialize a new empty store, require a pre-created empty private directory, or refuse every missing component?
options: Require the private data directory but create the database and internal subdirectories
Create the data directory and the whole empty store
Require the complete store layout to exist
open_points.default_guess: Require the installer to create the private data directory, then create the database and internal store layout on first open.

open_points.subject: canonical_values.canonical_bytes input representation
open_points.text: The operation takes “One JSON value” but must refuse “a duplicate key”. Once JSON text has already been parsed into an ordinary JSON object, duplicate keys are no longer observable.
open_points.question: Does `canonical_bytes` receive raw JSON text or a lossless parsed representation when duplicate-member detection is required, and which layer owns parsing?
options: Accept raw JSON bytes/text and parse with duplicate detection
Accept a lossless JSON syntax tree that preserves duplicate members
Make `surface` reject duplicates before passing an ordinary JSON value and remove that error from this operation
open_points.default_guess: Make `surface` parse with duplicate detection and pass an already valid JSON value; `canonical_bytes` then handles canonical encoding and non-finite numbers.

open_points.subject: JSON value size checks
open_points.text: `fit_port_value` takes a size bound and says it applies to “the whole value”, but does not state which byte representation is counted for a JSON value.
open_points.question: Are JSON value size limits measured using received request bytes, UTF-8 noncanonical serialization, or RFC 8785 canonical bytes?
options: RFC 8785 canonical byte length
Original received JSON byte length
A separately supplied stored-byte length
open_points.default_guess: Measure the RFC 8785 canonical bytes that are stored and hashed.

open_points.subject: effects.operation_element_conclusion across retries
open_points.text: The operation returns a conclusion “from the NodeExecution and EffectAttempt together”, but an element may have several NodeExecutions and EffectAttempts after `not_sent` or `not_applied` retries, and no selection rule is stated here.
open_points.question: Which attempt determines the current conclusion when an operation element has multiple attempts?
options: The greatest `attempt_number`
The latest record in store order
Combine all attempts by a separate precedence rule
open_points.default_guess: Use the greatest `attempt_number`, then combine that attempt's NodeExecution and EffectAttempt according to A11.

open_points.subject: flows.prove_flow_version failure result
open_points.text: It returns “the first failure with phase, node or edge and reason”, but the reason representation and closed set of reason values are not defined.
open_points.question: What exact reason identifiers and accompanying fields can a ProofResult failure return for each check in the nine proof phases?
options: A closed reason enumeration with phase-specific fields
A bounded free-text reason only
A structured reference to the failed normative check
open_points.default_guess: Use a closed reason enumeration, with structured node, edge, port or guard fields where applicable.

open_points.subject: store.page_records continuation under mutable filters
open_points.text: The continuation token is “the store position of the last item returned” and is bound to the record type and filter, while filterable lifecycle fields such as `status` change in place. The text only guarantees that “A record added meanwhile never shifts, repeats or hides an item.”
open_points.question: If records enter or leave a status filter between pages, is paging a snapshot of first-page membership or a live re-evaluation, and is a token still valid if its anchor record no longer matches the filter?
options: Live membership, using the stored position even if the anchor no longer matches
Snapshot membership fixed when the first page is issued
Invalidate the token when the anchor no longer belongs to the filtered list
open_points.default_guess: Use live membership below the stored position and keep the token valid as long as that store position still exists.
